  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

tools.name: mcp__1a59c906-04da-521d-bda7-7f71b9f9e01c__batch
tools.description: Create a doc, or apply several operations to one doc atomically.

tools.name: mcp__1a59c906-04da-521d-bda7-7f71b9f9e01c__guide
tools.description: Docs guides: topic.instructions repeats the server instructions. Read it only if your client dropped them. Also topic.<name>, refusal.<code>. After a doc's birth → ["topic.index"].

items.description: topic.<name> (instructions, index, editing, tabs, comments, charts, chart-definition, diagram, uploads, sharing, skill) or refusal.<code>; several per call is fine.

tools.name: mcp__1a59c906-04da-521d-bda7-7f71b9f9e01c__update
tools.description: Edit a tab's contents, rename a doc or tab, or change a stored value.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_pr__bind_pr
tools.description: Bind this session to a PR the PR bar did not pick up (fork remote, GitHub Enterprise host, PR opened elsewhere) by its URL. The repository must be this checkout's origin or one the user's sessions already have a PR bound from. Restores a dismissed open PR. The user is asked to approve (in auto mode the app may approve without asking, judging from the conversation, except to restore a PR the user dismissed; in bypass permissions mode it does not ask), so bind only a PR the user asked you to track.

url.description: The pull request URL, e.g. https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123.

_consent.description: Set by the app. Do not set it.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_pr__get_status
tools.description: Read the pull request bound to a Code session in this app (default "self") and its CI monitor: PR number/url/state/branches, CI check counts and failing check names, review decision, mergeability, and the auto_fix / auto_merge / auto_archive_on_close switches. Served from the app's cache. Use after `gh pr create` instead of polling `gh pr checks`.

session_id.description: The session to read: the literal string "self" (default) or a sessionId from ccd_session_mgmt list_sessions.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_pr__set_monitor
tools.description: Turn this session's CI monitor switches on or off for its bound, open PR (the CI popover's checkboxes). auto_fix: the app wakes this session with a `<ci-monitor-event>` on CI failures, merge conflicts and review comments. address_comments must equal auto_fix on this machine. auto_archive_on_close: archive this session once the PR merges or closes. Pass only the switches to change, and the PR's url with auto_fix. The user is asked to approve each call (in auto mode the app may approve without asking, and in bypass permissions mode it does not ask), so only call it when the user asked for that switch.

auto_fix.description: Wake this session on CI failures, merge conflicts and review comments.

address_comments.description: Review-comment delivery. On this machine it is the same switch as auto_fix and must equal it when passed.

auto_archive_on_close.description: Archive this session once its PR merges or closes.

url.description: The bound pull request's URL, as get_status reports it. Required with auto_fix.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a proposal you made with start_session (initiation "own_initiative" or "offer") that the user has not started.

Call this when it went stale: the work was done here after all (by you or the user), it turned out unnecessary, or you proposed a better-scoped replacement (propose the new one first, then dismiss the old task_id). A card the user answered has already left, "Do it here" included, so it needs no call.

task_id.description: The task_id the start_session proposal returned.

reason.description: Optional one-line reason the suggestion is no longer needed, e.g. "fixed in this session" or "superseded by task_ab12cd34".

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__hand_off_to_session
tools.description: Move the task you are in the middle of into its own session (a fork of this conversation plus your remaining plan) so you can answer the user now. Use it when a new user message about something else arrives mid-task — not for small corrections or when the user said to keep the work here. In a worktree the fork gets a fresh worktree, normally cut from your branch tip: commit first (uncommitted edits stay here). Bold title line and one sentence right before the call; after it, stop that task here and answer the new message — no recap.

title.description: Under 60 chars; names the task being moved.

remaining_plan.description: What is left to do: steps, files, what done looks like.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

title.description: Short noun-phrase title for the chapter (under 40 chars). Shown in the table of contents.

summary.description: Optional one-line summary of what this chapter covers. Shown on hover in the table of contents.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__read_widget_context
tools.description: Read context from an embedded interactive widget. Widgets are rendered alongside chat from prior tool calls and can be interacted with by the user. Call this when you need to know the current state of a widget.

tool_name.description: The name of the widget tool to get context for

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

items.description: The whole plan, in order (1–12 steps); replaces the previous list.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence; the detail goes in message. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

message.description: For a reply: what the click sends, up to 300 characters of plain text — no leading / or !. Omit when the label is the whole message.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__find
tools.description: Search the current page in the Browser pane for elements whose accessibility-tree line (role / name / text) contains `query`, case-insensitively. Returns up to 20 `ref_N` matches usable with `computer`/`form_input`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

query.description: Text to look for in an element's role, name or text (case-insensitive substring, e.g. "Sign in", "search", "Add to cart").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__form_input
tools.description: Set the value of a form element identified by `ref` (from read_page/find). Handles input/textarea/select/checkbox/contenteditable.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

ref.description: Element reference ID from the read_page tool (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2")

value.description: The value to set. For checkboxes use boolean, for selects use option value or text, for other inputs use appropriate string/number

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this form fill does on the page and to what, for example 'Sets the delivery date to 29 September'. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__get_page_text
tools.description: Extract the visible text of the Browser pane's page (article/main content first, falls back to body innerText).

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__javascript_tool
tools.description: Execute JavaScript in the Browser pane's page for DEBUGGING and INSPECTION only. Do NOT use this to implement UI changes — edit source code instead.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description: Action to perform (only `javascript_exec` is supported).

text.description: The JavaScript code to execute. Evaluated in the page context with REPL semantics: top-level `await` works, and the result of the last expression is returned automatically — write the expression you want (e.g. `window.myData.value`, or `await fetch(url).then(r=>r.json())`) rather than `return ...`. Return values are serialized as JSON.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__navigate
tools.description: Navigate the Browser pane to a URL, or go "back"/"forward" in history. If the Browser pane isn't open yet, this opens it at the URL (no dev server needed).

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

force.description: If the page shows a "Leave site?" dialog because of unsaved changes, discard those changes and navigate anyway. Defaults to false.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_list
tools.description: List servers started with preview_start. Returns serverIds for use with other preview_* tools.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_logs
tools.description: Get server stdout/stderr output. Use to check for build errors, verify server behavior, or read debug output. Use 'level' to filter to errors only, or 'search' to filter for specific text. Use after preview_start.

level.description: Filter by level: 'all' (default) shows all output, 'error' shows only lines containing error/exception/failed/fatal

search.description: Filter to lines containing this text (e.g., '[DEBUG]', 'POST /api')

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_start

url.description: URL to open in the Browser pane without a dev server (instead of starting one by `name`).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_stop
tools.description: Stop a server started with preview_start.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__read_console_messages
tools.description: Get console output (log, info, warn, error, debug) from the Browser pane.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__read_network_requests
tools.description: List network requests, or fetch a specific response body by `requestId`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

urlPattern.description: Substring filter on the request URL as listed (auth values show as REDACTED).

requestId.description: If provided, returns the response body for this request instead of listing.

limit.description: Max entries to return when listing (default: 50).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__read_page
tools.description: Read the current page in the Browser pane as a YAML-style accessibility tree. Each interactive element is tagged `[ref_N]` for use with `computer`/`form_input`/`find`. Prefer this over screenshot for verifying text and structure. Output is limited to 50000 characters by default; if it exceeds the limit it is truncated with a note — pass a larger max_chars, or use ref_id/depth to focus.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

filter.description: 'interactive' returns only clickable/typable elements; 'all' (default) returns the full tree.

ref_id.description: Restrict the tree to descendants of this `ref_N` (from a previous read_page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

content.content:
Fixes #2255
Fixes #2256

An `Entire-Checkpoint:` line anywhere in a commit message still decides which checkpoint a commit writes to. Main's provenance check (`stampedByAnotherCommit`) only refuses a checkpoint that already exists in the local store, so a checkpoint ID in a commit body, whether pasted, quoted, indented, or mentioned mid-sentence, still steers three writes.

This PR now also carries #2259 (the trailer writer fix). The stricter reader here is what makes that writer bug reachable, so the two need to land together, and I'm closing #2259 in favour of this one.

## Problem

I ported the scenarios onto current main and ran them there:

| Scenario on main | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| `entire attach` on a commit whose body says `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` | The attached session is written into `<id>`, which ends up holding two unrelated sessions. Same for an indented line and for "Follow-up to Entire-Checkpoint: <id> from last week." |
| `git commit -m` with that line in the body, `<id>` not in this clone | prepare-commit-msg treats it as already stamped and adds no trailer. Post-commit then condenses the session's work under `<id>`, claiming an ID that may belong to a teammate's unfetched checkpoint. |
| Same, `<id>` already in this clone | Post-commit correctly refuses to write there, but the commit ends up with no checkpoint at all. |
| `entire explain --commit <sha> --generate` | Resolves the first mention anywhere in the message. |

## Cause

Every place that decides "may I write to this checkpoint" reads trailers with `ParseCheckpoint`/`ParseAllCheckpoints`, whose regex is unanchored and scans the whole message. That is right for discovery, since squash commits carry their squashed commits' trailers in the body, and wrong for deciding a write.

## Fix

Only the final trailer block, read by git's grammar, decides a write:

- `stampedTrailer` (prepare-commit-msg and the agent fast path) and `stampedTrailersOf` (post-commit)
- the amend handler, which still treats a deleted ID mentioned anywhere as stripped, as main does
- attach's `planAttachLink` and `resolveCheckpointID`, switched together so joining and resolving agree
- explain's `--generate` paths, and the per-commit read-only views (`explain <commit>`, `explain --commit`, the export, and the review re-run guard), which now show the checkpoint `--generate` and attach use (`CommitCheckpoint`: the final block's last ID, falling back to the first ID anywhere only when the block names none)

Prepare reads the message as git will record it. Git runs its commit hooks with `GIT_EDITOR=:` when it opens no editor (githooks(5): `-m`/`-F` without `-e`, `--no-edit`, `-C`), which the source word cannot tell, since `-m -e` reports `message` and an amend reports `commit` either way. A message git opens loses the lines starting with git's comment prefix and everything from the exact scissors line down; any other keeps its comment lines, unless `commit.cleanup=strip`. Git's comment block is the run of comment lines after a blank line that ends the message, or the part above the scissors line, which can also start it. The prefix is `core.commentChar` or `core.commentString` (aliases, last one set wins), `#` when unset, and for `auto` it is read back from that block, checked against git's own rule, or, with no block (`commit.status=false`, no editor), picked by that rule: the first of `#;@!$%^&|:` that starts no line. Prepare then judges the final block as post-commit will read the recorded commit, by git's trailer grammar with `auto` read as `#`. Prepare writes its explanation and inherited trailers with the same prefix, so git's cleanup removes the explanation. Trailer lines accept `Key:value` and tab separators, as git does. The final-block reader rejects leading-whitespace pseudo-trailers, accepts indented lines only as continuations, never reads the subject paragraph as trailers, and skips lines starting with git's comment prefix, as git's trailer parser does. That last part matters because `commit.cleanup=scissors` and `whitespace` keep comment lines, so the recorded commit carries Entire's explanation right below its trailer. Post-commit, attach and `explain --generate` read a recorded commit with the configured prefix (`auto` reads as `#`, as in `git interpret-trailers`), and only look the prefix up when the message names a checkpoint that a read without it misses. The writer from #2259 joins only a trailer block without comment lines, so a trailer it appends is always one the readers accept.

Every trailer prepare adds to a message git opens goes above git's comment block, whether it is the template's, an amend's restored or fresh one, an agent's, or an inherited one, so `commit -v` cannot cut it off. Under `auto` with a cleanup that keeps comment lines, git's block would stay below the trailer where the grammar does not skip it, so the trailer goes below the block instead, above any scissors line. A message git does not open gets its trailer appended, so its own lines stay where the user put them (`-m "#42 fix login"`, `--amend --no-edit` of a body ending in a `#` paragraph). The template puts prepare's explanation in its own paragraph between the user's lines and the trailer: a subject typed on the line just above cannot join the trailer into the subject paragraph, and cleanup modes that keep comments leave the trailer as its own block. Like git, the reader also accepts a block holding a `Signed-off-by:` or `(cherry picked from commit …)` line with other lines in it, while trailers make up at least a quarter of the block. `explain --generate` writes into the block's last ID, the one attach joins, and when the only checkpoint lines sit outside the final block its error names them. Post-commit also accepts the trailer prepare left, stamped, restored or kept, wherever the user's edits moved it (a per-worktree marker tied to the commit's parent): prepare generated that ID or found it in the final block it was handed, so an ID pasted into the body cannot match it. prepare-commit-msg reads git's comment config once per hook.

The commit-msg hook's empty-message check now counts content the way git's cleanup will, from the same `GIT_EDITOR` signal: prefix lines count as comments only in a message git opened, or in every message under `commit.cleanup=strip`, which git applies to `-m` messages too, using the same comment prefix and exact scissors line. A `Signed-off-by:` line alone is not content, as in git's own check. Before, an untouched editor message with `core.commentChar=;` or `commit -v` was committed holding only the trailer instead of aborting, and `git commit -m "#42 fix login"` lost its trailer; both also happen on main.

Unchanged on purpose: read-only lookups that discover every checkpoint a commit mentions (resume, status, attribution, explain's history listings), squash and redo inheritance, and `RemoveCheckpointTrailers`, which stays broad so a delete removes every copy.

## Why nothing caught it

Main already stops a leftover mention of a deleted checkpoint from counting as the commit's own (`TestCheckpointDelete_LeftoverDeletedIDNeverReceivesNewWork`), by filtering through the deleted list. The same leftover naming a live or unfetched checkpoint was not covered, and attach and explain had no test with a body mention at all.

The branch's own tests then simulated git: they handed the hooks the message git would write and recorded commits with go-git, so they shared the code's assumptions about git's comment block and editor, and each review round found another git mode. `TestTrailerAuthority_RealGitCommits` now runs real `git commit` with Entire's hooks and a scripted editor.

## Tests, verified RED before the fix

Each failed on main's call sites (I merged main first) and passes now:

- **Body mentions:** `checkpoint_trailer_authority_test.go` (real hook binaries), `TestAttach_*DoesNotSelectCheckpoint` and `TestExplainGenerate_BodyCheckpointLineIsNotATrailer`. A pasted, indented or prose `Entire-Checkpoint:` line is no longer reused by prepare, joined by attach, or written by `explain --generate`.
- **Comment prefix and scissors:** `EditorCommitHonorsCommentChar`, `AmendHonorsCommentChar`, `ProseScissorsMarkerIsNotACut`, `UntouchedEditorMessageAborts` and `MessageSubjectStartingWithHashKeepsTrailer`. `;`, `auto`, `commit -v` and `-m "#42 …"` messages are read the way git cleans them.
- **Cleanup modes that keep comments:** `CleanupKeepingCommentsLinksTheCommit` and `TestAttach_TrailerFollowedByCommentLinesJoinsCheckpoint`. With `commit.cleanup=scissors` or `whitespace` the trailer still links the commit, as `git interpret-trailers` reads it.
- **Grammar:** `trailers_test.go` covers the subject paragraph, continuations, `Key:value` and tab separators, and comment lines.

`VerboseAmendKeepsItsTrailer` and `TestExplainReadOnly_FindsBodyCheckpointLine` are guards that pass before and after.

Review then found regressions in the stricter rule itself; these failed on the branch before their fix:

- **Trailers prepare adds:** `AddedTrailerSurvivesVerboseCleanup` (amend restore, amend after a delete, agent editor commit), `ClearedAmendMessageAborts`, `SubjectOnTheTemplatesSecondLineLinks`, the `auto` row of `CleanupKeepingCommentsLinksTheCommit`, and the `AnchorsToTheEndingBlock` unit tests. `UntouchedEditorMessageAborts` gains a `commit.status=false` guard.
- **Git's block rule and explain:** the cherry-pick and quarter-trailer cases in `trailers_test.go`, and `TestExplainGenerate_UsesTheLastFinalBlockTrailer`.
- **`commit.cleanup=strip` and scissors:** `StripCleanupMessageOfCommentsAborts`, and the CRLF scissors case in `trailers_test.go`, where git does not cut.

A second review round found more git modes; these failed on the branch before their fix:

- **Real git:** `TestTrailerAuthority_RealGitCommits`, 15 `git commit` cases across `-m`, `-m -e -v`, `-F`, the editor, `--amend`, `--amend --no-edit`, templates, `;`, `auto`, `commit.status=false` and the strip, whitespace and scissors cleanups. Each commit must end with exactly the trailer prepare left as its final block, stored by post-commit, keep the user's lines first, and abort when saved untouched. Before the fix, `-F` under `auto` got a second trailer, and a template under `auto` with whitespace cleanup ended with git's `;` block below its trailer.
- **Placement:** `NoEditAmendKeepsHashLinesInPlace` (the restored trailer landed above `#42 fix login`), `MessageEndingWithHashLinesKeepsItsParagraphs`, the `-m -e -v` row of `AddedTrailerSurvivesVerboseCleanup` (the trailer went below the diff), `BodyTypedBelowTheTrailerStillLinks` (agent fast path and amend keep), and the `AutoCommentPrefix` and `StampedTrailer` unit tests.
- **Readers:** `TestExplainReadOnly_ShowsTheLastFinalBlockTrailer`, `TestRunExplainExport_CommitExportsItsLastFinalTrailer` (it exported `aaaaaaaaaaaa` instead of `bbbbbbbbbbbb`) and `TestHeadCheckpointFlags_ReadsTheFinalBlockTrailer`. `TestExplainGenerate_BodyCheckpointLineIsNotATrailer` now expects the error to name the checkpoint.

Also added with these fixes: `EditedMessageSourceKeepsGitsBlockLast`, `MessageEndingWithHashLineLinks`, `BodyTypedBelowTemplatePromptStillLinks`, `AutoCommentCharWithoutStatusBlock` and `CommitMsgFollowsGitsEmptinessRules`.

A third review round: `TestTrailerAuthority_RealGitCommits` gains a `-t` template without a final newline under `auto` (git writes its comment block with no blank line above it, so Entire's explanation was kept) and now checks that git's default cleanup removes the explanation in every row that uses it; `TestAutoCommentPrefix` covers the same block.

## Rejected alternatives

- Anchoring the whole-message regex to line starts: a body line could still steer writes, and indented squash messages would stop being discovered.
- Checking only that the named checkpoint exists: existence says nothing about whether this commit stamped it, and it misses IDs this clone has not fetched.
- Guessing `auto` from the whole message: once git has written its comment block, the character it chose always looks used, so the guess is wrong. The prefix is read back from git's own block instead.
- Guessing whether git opened the editor from the source word or the message's shape: `-m -e` reports `message`, an amend reports `commit` either way, and a `-m` message can end with `#` lines that look like git's block. Git tells its hooks with `GIT_EDITOR=:`.
- Splitting the stricter reader from the placement fixes: the reader alone loses the link in every mode where main's writer leaves the trailer outside the final block, so they ship together.

## Known gap

A commit whose stamped trailer the user moves out of the final block in the editor, for example by typing a body below it, is still condensed into that checkpoint: post-commit accepts the trailer prepare left. Attach and `explain --generate` read only the final block, so they treat that commit as unlinked, and `--generate` names the out-of-block checkpoint in its error. Moving the trailer back would take a new step in commit-msg, so it is left out.

The hooks read git's `GIT_EDITOR=:` as "no editor". A `GIT_EDITOR=:` you export yourself looks the same, so such a commit gets its trailer after git's comment block (lost with `-v`), and a message saved untouched is recorded holding only the trailer instead of aborting.

`explain`'s history listings still match a commit by the first checkpoint ID in its message.

Squash and redo inheritance still scan the whole message of the squashed or reset commits, so an `Entire-Checkpoint:` mention in one of their bodies is carried into the new commit's final trailer block. Fixing it needs per-commit parsing of SQUASH_MSG and a rule for nested squashes, so it is left for a follow-up.

A GitHub "Squash and merge" commit joins the squashed messages without indentation, so its final block is the last squashed commit's trailer and attach joins that checkpoint, as on main. Telling it apart needs a way to recognize squash merges.

The hooks read `commit.cleanup` and `commit.status` from git config only, so `git commit --cleanup=<mode>`, `--status` and `--no-status` are invisible to them. Under `core.commentChar=auto` that can misplace the trailer: with `--cleanup=whitespace`, git's kept comment block ends the recorded commit below the trailer, so attach and `explain --generate` treat the commit as unlinked, while post-commit still condenses into the checkpoint prepare stamped.

## Branch history

This branch predates main's provenance model. Fixes #2255
Fixes #2256

An `Entire-Checkpoint:` line anywhere in a commit message still decides which checkpoint a commit writes to. Main's provenance check (`stampedByAnotherCommit`) only refuses a checkpoint that already exists in the local store, so a checkpoint ID in a commit body, whether pasted, quoted, indented, or mentioned mid-sentence, still steers three writes.

This PR now also carries #2259 (the trailer writer fix). The stricter reader here is what makes that writer bug reachable, so the two need to land together, and I'm closing #2259 in favour of this one.

## Problem

I ported the scenarios onto current main and ran them there:

| Scenario on main | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| `entire attach` on a commit whose body says `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` | The attached session is written into `<id>`, which ends up holding two unrelated sessions. Same for an indented line and for "Follow-up to Entire-Checkpoint: <id> from last week." |
| `git commit -m` with that line in the body, `<id>` not in this clone | prepare-commit-msg treats it as already stamped and adds no trailer. Post-commit then condenses the session's work under `<id>`, claiming an ID that may belong to a teammate's unfetched checkpoint. |
| Same, `<id>` already in this clone | Post-commit correctly refuses to write there, but the commit ends up with no checkpoint at all. |
| `entire explain --commit <sha> --generate` | Resolves the first mention anywhere in the message. |

## Cause

Every place that decides "may I write to this checkpoint" reads trailers with `ParseCheckpoint`/`ParseAllCheckpoints`, whose regex is unanchored and scans the whole message. That is right for discovery, since squash commits carry their squashed commits' trailers in the body, and wrong for deciding a write.

## Fix

Only the final trailer block, read by git's grammar, decides a write:

- `stampedTrailer` (prepare-commit-msg and the agent fast path) and `stampedTrailersOf` (post-commit)
- the amend handler, which still treats a deleted ID mentioned anywhere as stripped, as main does
- attach's `planAttachLink` and `resolveCheckpointID`, switched together so joining and resolving agree
- explain's `--generate` paths, and the per-commit read-only views (`explain <commit>`, `explain --commit`, the export, and the review re-run guard), which now show the checkpoint `--generate` and attach use (`CommitCheckpoint`: the final block's last ID, falling back to the first ID anywhere only when the block names none)

Prepare reads the message as git will record it. Git runs its commit hooks with `GIT_EDITOR=:` when it opens no editor (githooks(5): `-m`/`-F` without `-e`, `--no-edit`, `-C`), which the source word cannot tell, since `-m -e` reports `message` and an amend reports `commit` either way. A message git opens loses the lines starting with git's comment prefix and everything from the exact scissors line down; any other keeps its comment lines, unless `commit.cleanup=strip`. Git's comment block is the run of comment lines after a blank line that ends the message, or the part above the scissors line, which can also start it. The prefix is `core.commentChar` or `core.commentString` (aliases, last one set wins), `#` when unset, and for `auto` it is read back from that block, checked against git's own rule, or, with no block (`commit.status=false`, no editor), picked by that rule: the first of `#;@!$%^&|:` that starts no line. Prepare then judges the final block as post-commit will read the recorded commit, by git's trailer grammar with `auto` read as `#`. Prepare writes its explanation and inherited trailers with the same prefix, so git's cleanup removes the explanation. Trailer lines accept `Key:value` and tab separators, as git does. The final-block reader rejects leading-whitespace pseudo-trailers, accepts indented lines only as continuations, never reads the subject paragraph as trailers, and skips lines starting with git's comment prefix, as git's trailer parser does. That last part matters because `commit.cleanup=scissors` and `whitespace` keep comment lines, so the recorded commit carries Entire's explanation right below its trailer. Post-commit, attach and `explain --generate` read a recorded commit with the configured prefix (`auto` reads as `#`, as in `git interpret-trailers`), and only look the prefix up when the message names a checkpoint that a read without it misses. The writer from #2259 joins only a trailer block without comment lines, so a trailer it appends is always one the readers accept.

Every trailer prepare adds to a message git opens goes above git's comment block, whether it is the template's, an amend's restored or fresh one, an agent's, or an inherited one, so `commit -v` cannot cut it off. Under `auto` with a cleanup that keeps comment lines, git's block would stay below the trailer where the grammar does not skip it, so the trailer goes below the block instead, above any scissors line. A message git does not open gets its trailer appended, so its own lines stay where the user put them (`-m "#42 fix login"`, `--amend --no-edit` of a body ending in a `#` paragraph). The template puts prepare's explanation in its own paragraph between the user's lines and the trailer: a subject typed on the line just above cannot join the trailer into the subject paragraph, and cleanup modes that keep comments leave the trailer as its own block. Like git, the reader also accepts a block holding a `Signed-off-by:` or `(cherry picked from commit …)` line with other lines in it, while trailers make up at least a quarter of the block. `explain --generate` writes into the block's last ID, the one attach joins, and when the only checkpoint lines sit outside the final block its error names them. Post-commit also accepts the trailer prepare left, stamped, restored or kept, wherever the user's edits moved it (a per-worktree marker tied to the commit's parent): prepare generated that ID or found it in the final block it was handed, so an ID pasted into the body cannot match it. prepare-commit-msg reads git's comment config once per hook.

The commit-msg hook's empty-message check now counts content the way git's cleanup will, from the same `GIT_EDITOR` signal: prefix lines count as comments only in a message git opened, or in every message under `commit.cleanup=strip`, which git applies to `-m` messages too, using the same comment prefix and exact scissors line. A `Signed-off-by:` line alone is not content, as in git's own check. Before, an untouched editor message with `core.commentChar=;` or `commit -v` was committed holding only the trailer instead of aborting, and `git commit -m "#42 fix login"` lost its trailer; both also happen on main.

Unchanged on purpose: read-only lookups that discover every checkpoint a commit mentions (resume, status, attribution, explain's history listings), squash and redo inheritance, and `RemoveCheckpointTrailers`, which stays broad so a delete removes every copy.

## Why nothing caught it

Main already stops a leftover mention of a deleted checkpoint from counting as the commit's own (`TestCheckpointDelete_LeftoverDeletedIDNeverReceivesNewWork`), by filtering through the deleted list. The same leftover naming a live or unfetched checkpoint was not covered, and attach and explain had no test with a body mention at all.

The branch's own tests then simulated git: they handed the hooks the message git would write and recorded commits with go-git, so they shared the code's assumptions about git's comment block and editor, and each review round found another git mode. `TestTrailerAuthority_RealGitCommits` now runs real `git commit` with Entire's hooks and a scripted editor.

## Tests, verified RED before the fix

Each failed on main's call sites (I merged main first) and passes now:

- **Body mentions:** `checkpoint_trailer_authority_test.go` (real hook binaries), `TestAttach_*DoesNotSelectCheckpoint` and `TestExplainGenerate_BodyCheckpointLineIsNotATrailer`. A pasted, indented or prose `Entire-Checkpoint:` line is no longer reused by prepare, joined by attach, or written by `explain --generate`.
- **Comment prefix and scissors:** `EditorCommitHonorsCommentChar`, `AmendHonorsCommentChar`, `ProseScissorsMarkerIsNotACut`, `UntouchedEditorMessageAborts` and `MessageSubjectStartingWithHashKeepsTrailer`. `;`, `auto`, `commit -v` and `-m "#42 …"` messages are read the way git cleans them.
- **Cleanup modes that keep comments:** `CleanupKeepingCommentsLinksTheCommit` and `TestAttach_TrailerFollowedByCommentLinesJoinsCheckpoint`. With `commit.cleanup=scissors` or `whitespace` the trailer still links the commit, as `git interpret-trailers` reads it.
- **Grammar:** `trailers_test.go` covers the subject paragraph, continuations, `Key:value` and tab separators, and comment lines.

`VerboseAmendKeepsItsTrailer` and `TestExplainReadOnly_FindsBodyCheckpointLine` are guards that pass before and after.

Review then found regressions in the stricter rule itself; these failed on the branch before their fix:

- **Trailers prepare adds:** `AddedTrailerSurvivesVerboseCleanup` (amend restore, amend after a delete, agent editor commit), `ClearedAmendMessageAborts`, `SubjectOnTheTemplatesSecondLineLinks`, the `auto` row of `CleanupKeepingCommentsLinksTheCommit`, and the `AnchorsToTheEndingBlock` unit tests. `UntouchedEditorMessageAborts` gains a `commit.status=false` guard.
- **Git's block rule and explain:** the cherry-pick and quarter-trailer cases in `trailers_test.go`, and `TestExplainGenerate_UsesTheLastFinalBlockTrailer`.
- **`commit.cleanup=strip` and scissors:** `StripCleanupMessageOfCommentsAborts`, and the CRLF scissors case in `trailers_test.go`, where git does not cut.

A second review round found more git modes; these failed on the branch before their fix:

- **Real git:** `TestTrailerAuthority_RealGitCommits`, 15 `git commit` cases across `-m`, `-m -e -v`, `-F`, the editor, `--amend`, `--amend --no-edit`, templates, `;`, `auto`, `commit.status=false` and the strip, whitespace and scissors cleanups. Each commit must end with exactly the trailer prepare left as its final block, stored by post-commit, keep the user's lines first, and abort when saved untouched. Before the fix, `-F` under `auto` got a second trailer, and a template under `auto` with whitespace cleanup ended with git's `;` block below its trailer.
- **Placement:** `NoEditAmendKeepsHashLinesInPlace` (the restored trailer landed above `#42 fix login`), `MessageEndingWithHashLinesKeepsItsParagraphs`, the `-m -e -v` row of `AddedTrailerSurvivesVerboseCleanup` (the trailer went below the diff), `BodyTypedBelowTheTrailerStillLinks` (agent fast path and amend keep), and the `AutoCommentPrefix` and `StampedTrailer` unit tests.

- Anchoring the whole-message regex to line starts: a body line could still steer writes, and indented squash messages would stop being discovered.
- Checking only that the named checkpoint exists: existence says nothing about whether this commit stamped it, and it misses IDs this clone has not fetched.
- Guessing `auto` from the whole message: once git has written its comment block, the character it chose always looks used, so the guess is wrong. The prefix is read back from git's own block instead.

A commit whose stamped trailer the user moves out of the final block in the editor, for example by typing a body below it, is still condensed into that checkpoint: post-commit accepts the trailer prepare left. ("That last part matters because `commit.cleanup=scissors` and `whitespace` keep comment lines, so the recorded commit carries Entire's explanation right below its trailer.",

("The writer from #2259 joins only a trailer block without comment lines, so a trailer it appends is always one the readers accept.",

("The template puts prepare's explanation in its own paragraph between the user's lines and the trailer: a subject typed on the line just above cannot join the trailer into the subject paragraph, and cleanup modes that keep comments leave the trailer as its own block.",
 "The template puts prepare's explanation in its own paragraph between the user's lines and the trailer, so a subject typed on the line just above cannot join the trailer into the subject paragraph."),
("Post-commit also accepts the trailer prepare left, stamped, restored or kept, wherever the user's edits moved it (a per-worktree marker tied to the commit's parent): prepare generated that ID or found it in the final block it was handed, so an ID pasted into the body cannot match it. prepare-commit-msg reads git's comment config once per hook.",
 "Squash and redo inheritance add each inherited trailer to the final block unless that block already names it: git seeds an editor squash message with the squashed commits' messages, their trailers indented in the body, which do not count. ("Unchanged on purpose: read-only lookups that discover every checkpoint a commit mentions (resume, status, attribution, explain's history listings), squash and redo inheritance, and `RemoveCheckpointTrailers`, which stays broad so a delete removes every copy.",

A fourth review round; each of these failed on the branch before its fix:

- **Moved trailers:** `TrailerTheUserMovesOutOfTheFinalBlockUnlinks` (an agent commit and an amend, with a body typed below the trailer or the trailer commented out under whitespace cleanup): post-commit must not condense into a trailer attach and explain read as unlinked.

- **Inheritance:** `SquashDefaultMessageLinksInheritedTrailerInTheFinalBlock` and `RedoTrailerQuotedInTheBodyLinksInTheFinalBlock`.
- **Explain:** `REDACTED`.
- **Hook caches:** `TestGetGitDir_HookDoesNotCacheAFailure` and `TestGitCommentConfig_HookDoesNotCacheAReadUnderADoneContext`.'''

old_gap_end=s.index("## Branch history\n")
gap='''## Known gap

A body typed below the trailer in the editor moves it out of the final block, so the commit is unlinked, as `git interpret-trailers` reads it, and `entire attach` can link it afterwards. Moving the trailer back would take a new step in commit-msg, so it is left out.

The hooks read git's `GIT_EDITOR=:` as "no editor". A `GIT_EDITOR=:` you export yourself looks the same, so such a commit gets its trailer after git's comment block (lost with `-v`), and a message saved untouched is recorded holding only the trailer instead of aborting.

Squash and redo inheritance still take their IDs from the whole message of the squashed or reset commits, so an `Entire-Checkpoint:` mention in one of their bodies is carried into the new commit's final trailer block. Fixing it needs per-commit parsing of SQUASH_MSG and a rule for nested squashes, so it is left for a follow-up.

A GitHub "Squash and merge" commit joins the squashed messages without indentation, so its final block is the last squashed commit's trailer and attach joins that checkpoint, as on main. Telling it apart needs a way to recognize squash merges.

The hooks read `commit.cleanup` and `commit.status` from git config only, so `git commit --cleanup=<mode>`, `--status` and `--no-status` are invisible to them. With `--cleanup=whitespace`, prepare still writes its explanation, which git records with the prompt it quotes, and under `core.commentChar=auto` git's kept comment block can end the recorded commit below the trailer, leaving the commit unlinked.

An `Entire-Checkpoint : <id>` line, spaced before its colon, is a checkpoint trailer to git but not to Entire's readers. Changing that touches every checkpoint ID reader.

Fixes #2255
Fixes #2256

An `Entire-Checkpoint:` line anywhere in a commit message still decides which checkpoint a commit writes to. Main's provenance check (`stampedByAnotherCommit`) only refuses a checkpoint that already exists in the local store, so a checkpoint ID in a commit body, whether pasted, quoted, indented, or mentioned mid-sentence, still steers three writes.

This PR now also carries #2259 (the trailer writer fix). The stricter reader here is what makes that writer bug reachable, so the two need to land together, and I'm closing #2259 in favour of this one.

## Problem

I ported the scenarios onto current main and ran them there:

| Scenario on main | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| `entire attach` on a commit whose body says `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` | The attached session is written into `<id>`, which ends up holding two unrelated sessions. Same for an indented line and for "Follow-up to Entire-Checkpoint: <id> from last week." |
| `git commit -m` with that line in the body, `<id>` not in this clone | prepare-commit-msg treats it as already stamped and adds no trailer. Post-commit then condenses the session's work under `<id>`, claiming an ID that may belong to a teammate's unfetched checkpoint. |
| Same, `<id>` already in this clone | Post-commit correctly refuses to write there, but the commit ends up with no checkpoint at all. |
| `entire explain --commit <sha> --generate` | Resolves the first mention anywhere in the message. |

## Cause

Every place that decides "may I write to this checkpoint" reads trailers with `ParseCheckpoint`/`ParseAllCheckpoints`, whose regex is unanchored and scans the whole message. That is right for discovery, since squash commits carry their squashed commits' trailers in the body, and wrong for deciding a write.

## Fix

Only the final trailer block, read by git's grammar, decides a write:

- `stampedTrailer` (prepare-commit-msg and the agent fast path) and `stampedTrailersOf` (post-commit)
- the amend handler, which still treats a deleted ID mentioned anywhere as stripped, as main does
- attach's `planAttachLink` and `resolveCheckpointID`, switched together so joining and resolving agree
- explain's `--generate` paths, and the read-only views (`explain <commit>`, `explain --commit`, the branch listing, the export, and the review re-run guard), which now show the checkpoint `--generate` and attach use (`CommitCheckpoint`: the final block's last ID, falling back to the first ID anywhere only when the block names none). `explain --checkpoint` finds every commit that names the checkpoint, so a squash commit is found by its inherited and its stamped ID

Prepare reads the message as git will record it. Git runs its commit hooks with `GIT_EDITOR=:` when it opens no editor (githooks(5): `-m`/`-F` without `-e`, `--no-edit`, `-C`), which the source word cannot tell, since `-m -e` reports `message` and an amend reports `commit` either way. A message git opens loses the lines starting with git's comment prefix and everything from the exact scissors line down; any other keeps its comment lines, unless `commit.cleanup=strip`. Git's comment block is the run of comment lines after a blank line that ends the message, or the part above the scissors line, which can also start it. The prefix is `core.commentChar` or `core.commentString` (aliases, last one set wins), `#` when unset, and for `auto` it is read back from that block, checked against git's own rule, or, with no block (`commit.status=false`, no editor), picked by that rule: the first of `#;@!$%^&|:` that starts no line. Prepare then judges the final block as post-commit will read the recorded commit, by git's trailer grammar with `auto` read as `#`. Prepare writes its explanation with the same prefix, and only into a message whose comment lines git's cleanup drops: under `whitespace`, `verbatim` or `scissors` cleanup git would record it, and the prompt it quotes, so prepare writes none there. Trailer lines accept what git accepts: a key of letters, digits and dashes, optional spaces or tabs before the colon (`Reviewed-by : Bob`), and `Key:value` and tab separators. The final-block reader rejects leading-whitespace pseudo-trailers, accepts indented lines only as continuations, never reads the subject paragraph as trailers, and skips lines starting with git's comment prefix, as git's trailer parser does. That last part matters because `commit.cleanup=scissors` and `whitespace` keep comment lines, such as git's own block below the trailer. Post-commit, attach and `explain --generate` read a recorded commit with the configured prefix (`auto` reads as `#`, as in `git interpret-trailers`), and only look the prefix up when the message names a checkpoint that a read without it misses. The writer from #2259 joins any final paragraph that is a trailer block read without a comment prefix, the strictest reading, so a trailer it appends is always one the readers accept, and a mixed block (a `Signed-off-by:` line beside a note) keeps the user's trailers in the final block instead of being pushed out by a new paragraph.

Every trailer prepare adds to a message git opens goes above git's comment block, whether it is the template's, an amend's restored or fresh one, an agent's, or an inherited one, so `commit -v` cannot cut it off. Under `auto` with a cleanup that keeps comment lines, git's block would stay below the trailer where the grammar does not skip it, so the trailer goes below the block instead, above any scissors line. A message git does not open gets its trailer appended, so its own lines stay where the user put them (`-m "#42 fix login"`, `--amend --no-edit` of a body ending in a `#` paragraph). The template puts prepare's explanation in its own paragraph between the user's lines and the trailer, so a subject typed on the line just above cannot join the trailer into the subject paragraph. Like git, the reader also accepts a block holding a `Signed-off-by:` or `(cherry picked from commit …)` line with other lines in it, while trailers make up at least a quarter of the block. `explain --generate` writes into the block's last ID, the one attach joins, and when the only checkpoint lines sit outside the final block its error names them. Squash and redo inheritance add each inherited trailer to the final block unless that block already names it: git seeds an editor squash message with the squashed commits' messages, their trailers indented in the body, which do not count. A trailer the user's edits move out of the final block (a body typed below it, or the line commented out under a cleanup that keeps comments) no longer links the commit, for post-commit as for attach and explain. Each commit hook reads git's comment config and git dir once, caching only a successful read.

The commit-msg hook's empty-message check now counts content the way git's cleanup will, from the same `GIT_EDITOR` signal: prefix lines count as comments only in a message git opened, or in every message under `commit.cleanup=strip`, which git applies to `-m` messages too, using the same comment prefix and exact scissors line. A `Signed-off-by:` line alone is not content, as in git's own check. Before, an untouched editor message with `core.commentChar=;` or `commit -v` was committed holding only the trailer instead of aborting, and `git commit -m "#42 fix login"` lost its trailer; both also happen on main.

Unchanged on purpose: read-only lookups that discover every checkpoint a commit mentions (resume, status, attribution, `explain --checkpoint`), the sources squash and redo inheritance take their IDs from (the whole SQUASH_MSG and the redone commits' messages), and `RemoveCheckpointTrailers`, which stays broad so a delete removes every copy.

## Why nothing caught it

Main already stops a leftover mention of a deleted checkpoint from counting as the commit's own (`TestCheckpointDelete_LeftoverDeletedIDNeverReceivesNewWork`), by filtering through the deleted list. The same leftover naming a live or unfetched checkpoint was not covered, and attach and explain had no test with a body mention at all.

The branch's own tests then simulated git: they handed the hooks the message git would write and recorded commits with go-git, so they shared the code's assumptions about git's comment block and editor, and each review round found another git mode. `TestTrailerAuthority_RealGitCommits` now runs real `git commit` with Entire's hooks and a scripted editor.

## Tests, verified RED before the fix

Each failed on main's call sites (I merged main first) and passes now:

- **Body mentions:** `checkpoint_trailer_authority_test.go` (real hook binaries), `TestAttach_*DoesNotSelectCheckpoint` and `TestExplainGenerate_BodyCheckpointLineIsNotATrailer`. A pasted, indented or prose `Entire-Checkpoint:` line is no longer reused by prepare, joined by attach, or written by `explain --generate`.
- **Comment prefix and scissors:** `EditorCommitHonorsCommentChar`, `AmendHonorsCommentChar`, `ProseScissorsMarkerIsNotACut`, `UntouchedEditorMessageAborts` and `MessageSubjectStartingWithHashKeepsTrailer`. `;`, `auto`, `commit -v` and `-m "#42 …"` messages are read the way git cleans them.
- **Cleanup modes that keep comments:** `CleanupKeepingCommentsLinksTheCommit` and `TestAttach_TrailerFollowedByCommentLinesJoinsCheckpoint`. With `commit.cleanup=scissors` or `whitespace` the trailer still links the commit, as `git interpret-trailers` reads it.
- **Grammar:** `trailers_test.go` covers the subject paragraph, continuations, `Key:value` and tab separators, and comment lines.

`VerboseAmendKeepsItsTrailer` and `TestExplainReadOnly_FindsBodyCheckpointLine` are guards that pass before and after.

Review then found regressions in the stricter rule itself; these failed on the branch before their fix:

- **Trailers prepare adds:** `AddedTrailerSurvivesVerboseCleanup` (amend restore, amend after a delete, agent editor commit), `ClearedAmendMessageAborts`, `SubjectOnTheTemplatesSecondLineLinks`, the `auto` row of `CleanupKeepingCommentsLinksTheCommit`, and the `AnchorsToTheEndingBlock` unit tests. `UntouchedEditorMessageAborts` gains a `commit.status=false` guard.
- **Git's block rule and explain:** the cherry-pick and quarter-trailer cases in `trailers_test.go`, and `TestExplainGenerate_UsesTheLastFinalBlockTrailer`.
- **`commit.cleanup=strip` and scissors:** `StripCleanupMessageOfCommentsAborts`, and the CRLF scissors case in `trailers_test.go`, where git does not cut.

A second review round found more git modes; these failed on the branch before their fix:

- **Real git:** `TestTrailerAuthority_RealGitCommits`, 15 `git commit` cases across `-m`, `-m -e -v`, `-F`, the editor, `--amend`, `--amend --no-edit`, templates, `;`, `auto`, `commit.status=false` and the strip, whitespace and scissors cleanups. Each commit must end with exactly the trailer prepare left as its final block, stored by post-commit, keep the user's lines first, and abort when saved untouched. Before the fix, `-F` under `auto` got a second trailer, and a template under `auto` with whitespace cleanup ended with git's `;` block below its trailer.
- **Placement:** `NoEditAmendKeepsHashLinesInPlace` (the restored trailer landed above `#42 fix login`), `MessageEndingWithHashLinesKeepsItsParagraphs`, the `-m -e -v` row of `AddedTrailerSurvivesVerboseCleanup` (the trailer went below the diff), and the `AutoCommentPrefix` and `StampedTrailer` unit tests.
- **Readers:** `TestExplainReadOnly_ShowsTheLastFinalBlockTrailer`, `TestRunExplainExport_CommitExportsItsLastFinalTrailer` (it exported `aaaaaaaaaaaa` instead of `bbbbbbbbbbbb`) and `TestHeadCheckpointFlags_ReadsTheFinalBlockTrailer`. `TestExplainGenerate_BodyCheckpointLineIsNotATrailer` now expects the error to name the checkpoint.

Also added with these fixes: `EditedMessageSourceKeepsGitsBlockLast`, `MessageEndingWithHashLineLinks`, `BodyTypedBelowTemplatePromptStillLinks`, `AutoCommentCharWithoutStatusBlock` and `CommitMsgFollowsGitsEmptinessRules`.

A third review round: `TestTrailerAuthority_RealGitCommits` gains a `-t` template without a final newline under `auto` (git writes its comment block with no blank line above it, so Entire's explanation was kept) and now checks that git's default cleanup removes the explanation in every row that uses it; `TestAutoCommentPrefix` covers the same block.

A fourth review round; each of these failed on the branch before its fix:

- **Prompt in history:** `TestTrailerAuthority_RealGitCommits` gains editor rows for `whitespace`, `scissors` and `verbatim` cleanup, and every row now checks that the recorded commit holds neither Entire's explanation nor the `Last Prompt:` line. The existing template row under `auto` with scissors cleanup failed that check too.
- **Moved trailers:** `TrailerTheUserMovesOutOfTheFinalBlockUnlinks` (an agent commit and an amend, with a body typed below the trailer or the trailer commented out under whitespace cleanup): post-commit must not condense into a trailer attach and explain read as unlinked.
- **Writer and grammar:** the mixed-block rows of `TestAppendCheckpointTrailer`, and `Key : value`, digit-first and dash-first keys in `TestIsTrailerLine` and `TestParseAllCheckpointsFromFinalTrailerBlock`.
- **Inheritance:** `SquashDefaultMessageLinksInheritedTrailerInTheFinalBlock` and `RedoTrailerQuotedInTheBodyLinksInTheFinalBlock`.
- **Explain:** `REDACTED`.
- **Hook caches:** `TestGetGitDir_HookDoesNotCacheAFailure` and `TestGitCommentConfig_HookDoesNotCacheAReadUnderADoneContext`.

## Rejected alternatives

- Anchoring the whole-message regex to line starts: a body line could still steer writes, and indented squash messages would stop being discovered.
- Checking only that the named checkpoint exists: existence says nothing about whether this commit stamped it, and it misses IDs this clone has not fetched.
- Guessing `auto` from the whole message: once git has written its comment block, the character it chose always looks used, so the guess is wrong. The prefix is read back from git's own block instead.
- Guessing whether git opened the editor from the source word or the message's shape: `-m -e` reports `message`, an amend reports `commit` either way, and a `-m` message can end with `#` lines that look like git's block. Git tells its hooks with `GIT_EDITOR=:`.
- Splitting the stricter reader from the placement fixes: the reader alone loses the link in every mode where main's writer leaves the trailer outside the final block, so they ship together.

## Known gap

A body typed below the trailer in the editor moves it out of the final block, so the commit is unlinked, as `git interpret-trailers` reads it, and `entire attach` can link it afterwards. Moving the trailer back would take a new step in commit-msg, so it is left out.

The hooks read git's `GIT_EDITOR=:` as "no editor". A `GIT_EDITOR=:` you export yourself looks the same, so such a commit gets its trailer after git's comment block (lost with `-v`), and a message saved untouched is recorded holding only the trailer instead of aborting.

Squash and redo inheritance still take their IDs from the whole message of the squashed or reset commits, so an `Entire-Checkpoint:` mention in one of their bodies is carried into the new commit's final trailer block. Fixing it needs per-commit parsing of SQUASH_MSG and a rule for nested squashes, so it is left for a follow-up.

A GitHub "Squash and merge" commit joins the squashed messages without indentation, so its final block is the last squashed commit's trailer and attach joins that checkpoint, as on main. Telling it apart needs a way to recognize squash merges.

The hooks read `commit.cleanup` and `commit.status` from git config only, so `git commit --cleanup=<mode>`, `--status` and `--no-status` are invisible to them. With `--cleanup=whitespace`, prepare still writes its explanation, which git records with the prompt it quotes, and under `core.commentChar=auto` git's kept comment block can end the recorded commit below the trailer, leaving the commit unlinked.

An `Entire-Checkpoint : <id>` line, spaced before its colon, is a checkpoint trailer to git but not to Entire's readers. Changing that touches every checkpoint ID reader.

## Branch history

This branch predates main's provenance model. I merged current main, resolved every call-site conflict to main's version (the legacy migration this PR used to touch is gone), and re-applied the final-block reads to main's call sites in the last commit. The diff against main is the change to review.

## Test plan

- [x] `mise run check`: fmt, lint and all CI tests pass
- [x] real `git commit` across modes and configs, now automated as `TestTrailerAuthority_RealGitCommits`
- [ ] CI on ef0d61160

- Guessing `auto` from the whole message: once git has written its comment block, the character it chose always looks used, so the guess is wrong. The prefix is read back from git's own block instead.
- Guessing whether git opened the editor from the source word or the message's shape: `-m -e` reports `message`, an amend reports `commit` either way, and a `-m` message can end with `#` lines that look like git's block. Git tells its hooks with `GIT_EDITOR=:`.
- Splitting the stricter reader from the placement fixes: the reader alone loses the link in every mode where main's writer leaves the trailer outside the final block, so they ship together.

## Known gap

A body typed below the trailer in the editor moves it out of the final block, so the commit is unlinked, as `git interpret-trailers` reads it, and `entire attach` can link it afterwards. Moving the trailer back would take a new step in commit-msg, so it is left out.

The hooks read git's `GIT_EDITOR=:` as "no editor". A `GIT_EDITOR=:` you export yourself looks the same, so such a commit gets its trailer after git's comment block (lost with `-v`), and a message saved untouched is recorded holding only the trailer instead of aborting.

Squash and redo inheritance still take their IDs from the whole message of the squashed or reset commits, so an `Entire-Checkpoint:` mention in one of their bodies is carried into the new commit's final trailer block. Fixing it needs per-commit parsing of SQUASH_MSG and a rule for nested squashes, so it is left for a follow-up.

A GitHub "Squash and merge" commit joins the squashed messages without indentation, so its final block is the last squashed commit's trailer and attach joins that checkpoint, as on main. Telling it apart needs a way to recognize squash merges.

The hooks read `commit.cleanup` and `commit.status` from git config only, so `git commit --cleanup=<mode>`, `--status` and `--no-status` are invisible to them. With `--cleanup=whitespace`, prepare still writes its explanation, which git records with the prompt it quotes, and under `core.commentChar=auto` git's kept comment block can end the recorded commit below the trailer, leaving the commit unlinked.

An `Entire-Checkpoint : <id>` line, spaced before its colon, is a checkpoint trailer to git but not to Entire's readers. Changing that touches every checkpoint ID reader.

## Branch history

This branch predates main's provenance model. I merged current main, resolved every call-site conflict to main's version (the legacy migration this PR used to touch is gone), and re-applied the final-block reads to main's call sites after the merge. The diff against main is the change to review.

In entireio/cli the quality bar is *evidence*, not code volume. Stefan Haubold (`Soph`) wrote 25 of the last 60 commits as of 2026-08-14 and sets the house style. Diffs are often tiny (#1985 was +6/-1); PR bodies are lab notebooks.

The beat order every exemplar PR follows: **Problem** (failure quoted verbatim, real log/CI output) → **Cause** (traced to a specific commit, often by diffing logs from the last green run) → **Fix** (framed as removing an asymmetry, reusing an existing helper, not adding a mechanism) → **Why nothing caught it** (explicit coverage-gap post-mortem) → **Tests, "Verified RED"** (named tests plus the exact pre-fix failure message) → **Rejected alternatives** (with cost, e.g. "~4 signatures and ~45 call sites") → **Test plan checkboxes** ending in `mise run check`.

Two habits worth copying: performance claims use **interleaved** A/B runs with medians (sequential runs let the first arm absorb cold page-cache cost and invert the result — stated in both #1985 and #1968), and negative/deflated results get reported honestly (#1985 talked itself down from a 49% headline to 2%).

**Why:** matching this format is the highest-leverage thing for getting contributions merged fast, and it is doable before deep Go fluency.
**How to apply:** write the failing test first so its real output becomes the "Verified RED" line — the test discipline and the PR-body discipline are the same act.
